speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of your high blood pressure, how old are you, and have you noticed any headaches, visual changes, or nosebleeds recently?

text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: I notice he is a 5-year-old boy with systemic hypertension. To narrow down the cause, does he have any history of renal disease, abdominal pain, or changes in urinary habits?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the patient have weak or delayed femoral pulses compared to the brachial pulses, and is there a blood pressure difference between the arms and legs? I need to assess for coarctation of the aorta.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Doctor
text: Let me check his pulses and blood pressure in all four extremities to see if there is a significant gradient between the upper and lower body. I will also listen for a systolic murmur over the left infraclavicular area and the back. REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Echocardiogram findings indicate narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal.

speaker: Patient
text: All systems review is essentially negative as reported by the mother. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That assessment seems inconsistent with isolated upper extremity hypertension in a 5-year-old; migraines do not cause high blood pressure. I must urgently evaluate for coarctation of the aorta or renal artery stenosis, so I will request an abdominal ultrasound to rule out renal causes. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the abdominal ultrasound is normal, coarctation of the aorta remains the primary suspect for upper extremity hypertension. REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram
